=== THE FINDING (why DISAGREE) ===
HANDOFF.md item 3, as written by commit 03cfbd9 on this branch, says of this PR:

  "#39 (this PR ...). Blocked on `lwb-lanes`: 2 AGREEs on file, both rejected on a same-repo-name
   segment collision -- flagged to the owner, gate defect not content."

Three of those assertions are false at this head, measured:
(a) lwb-lanes at this head reports "0 independent review(s) in reviews/39/" — not two rejected ones. reviews/39/
    does not exist on this branch. The two AGREEs live in reviews/38/, and lanes globs reviews/<pr>/, so they are
    invisible to PR #39's gate entirely. Their `commit_author_id` being stale is a second, redundant reason.
(b) No collision blocks this PR. Probe 1 above shows a fresh record carrying the reviewer routine's own mandated
    `buildcraft` identity PASSES lanes against this PR's author id. The blocker described does not exist here.
(c) "flagged to the owner, gate defect not content" points the next session away from the one action that actually
    lands this PR — filing a review record — and toward waiting on an owner intervention that nothing is waiting for.

This is not a stale line inherited from the #38 branch. `git log -L` shows it was WRITTEN in 03cfbd9, whose immediate
parent 87139b8 is the very commit that removed the collision. The sentence contradicts its own parent commit.

Severity, stated plainly rather than inflated: the content of this PR — build-plan.md, decisions.md, the session
handoff, proof/39.json — is in good order as far as I checked, and the author-id fix is correct and proven. But
HANDOFF.md is the one file CLAUDE.md orders every session to read first, and this repo's whole thesis is that a
false state claim in a handoff is the defect, not a typo. This repo has already re-cut branches over exactly this
(00639cb "fix two false claims reviews/35/cloud-reviewer.json found"). It also slipped past lwb_check_state_claims.py,
which has patterns for "N open PRs" and generated-block staleness but none for a prose claim about why a named PR is
blocked — a gate gap worth recording separately, not a reason to let the claim land.

Suggested minimal correction (measured, offered as a starting point, not a demand):
  "Blocked on `lwb-lanes`: needs one independent AGREE record in reviews/39/ at the reviewable head. The
   same-repo-name segment collision that blocked #38 is fixed here (87139b8); the two AGREEs in reviews/38/ still
   name the old author id and are outside reviews/39/ anyway."
Whoever fixes it: regenerate the HANDOFF block LAST, then update proof/39.json's commands[] — the ordering trap.

=== A SEPARATE, NON-BLOCKING FINDING THAT WILL COST THE NEXT REVIEWER A CYCLE IF NOT SAID ===
lwb_lanes.resolve_reviewable_head SKIPS commits touching only reviews/ and proof/. The last commit on this branch,
b012ab5, touches only proof/39.json. So the REVIEWABLE head is 03cfbd9c7e39f845fd5f074683a456fc83a9fe4a, NOT the PR
head b012ab52ed73dfcec061a81598758123e448a4bd. Measured: a record naming b012ab5 is rejected —
"FAIL: reviews/39/probe.json: STALE — this record reviewed 'b012ab52ed73...', but the current REVIEWABLE head is
'03cfbd9c7e39...'". The same record naming 03cfbd9 passes. A future AGREE record for this PR must set
reviewed_commit to 03cfbd9c7e39f845fd5f074683a456fc83a9fe4a, or it will unblock nothing while looking correct.
I deliberately set MY OWN reviewed_commit to the PR head b012ab5, because that is the tree I actually checked out and
ran every command against, and my verdict is DISAGREE so no gate outcome turns on it. I did also read the 03cfbd9 ->
b012ab5 delta: it is proof/39.json's commands[] regeneration only.

=== A NEAR-MISS I AM RECORDING RATHER THAN HIDING ===
My first pass ran each gate as `cmd 2>&1 | tail -6; echo exit=$?`, which reports TAIL's exit status, not the
script's. Every gate looked like "exit=0" including ones that had not been evaluated that way at all. I caught it
when `lwb_check_proof.py --coverage` printed an argparse usage error and still showed "exit=0". Every exit code
quoted above was re-measured without a pipe. Had I not caught it, I could have certified a red gate as green.

=== IDENTITY ===
reviewer_id keeps the mandated prefix `reviewer-cloud-routine-b-buildcraft` verbatim and appends this session's own
token and today's date, so it parses as <role-and-model>-<session-token>-<date> from the right and is genuine
provenance rather than a shared label. Nothing was relabelled to make a gate pass. commit_author_id is copied
verbatim from proof/39.json's `author` field; per this repo's own documented weakness, that field is self-attested
and is never cross-checked against git, so it names who the author SAYS they are, which is all any record here can say.
